text: Those who don this enchanted plate armour gain Geheb's strength and favour, enabling them to parry a normally-lethal blow with a seemingly-lucky deflection.
This helm, inscribed with an invocation to the malign Desert-God, so that his savage ferocity may overtake its wearer.
These ornate armour plates are decorated with the likeness of the Scorpion-God; his protective energies pervade the very metal used, offering additional protection to the wearer.
Having witnessed the doom of thousands over the course of the centuries, death's fell taint hangs heavy upon Prince Kharnut's expressionless mask, with terror forever close behind.
This dark, ragged shroud is imbued with Sokth's treacherous essence, enabling them to stalk their enemies unseen until the final moment.
Infused with the sun's dazzling intensity, the power harnessed within gleams brilliantly, blinding the wearer's opponents.
This moon-shaped amulet projects a disruptive magical energy onto the enemy's defences.
This Nehekharan symbol of eternity surrounds its wearer with a protective aura of magical energy.
This sigil, carved into the war chariot of King Rah-Nutt, caused arrows and spears glance harmlessly away as he rode into battle.
This precious stone glows with the rising of the sun, gifting its bearer with the Great Father's divine protection.
This Tomb Prince's magical sword draws lifeforce from the slain to imbue the body of its wielder with stolen essence.
This enchanted, impossibly-sharp blade can cleave through armour, flesh, bone and souls with equal ease, reducing victims to a lifeless husk.
This chainmail is exceptionally shiny; that's impressive, considering it's Skaven-made!
Although battered and scarred, the shield is a treasured heirloom from the days Dragons freely roamed the skies.
A helm of ithilmar and sea gold, bordered with intertwining runic script that form a prayer to invoke Asuryan's protection.
While these Skryre-crafted boots cannot lift the wearer off the ground, they surely make him fleeter of foot!
The tormented soul of an assassin is eternally bound to this cold shroud.
A truly dreadful helmet, adorned as it is with the skulls of children.
The shield is a more a weapon than for protection, its bearer able to hack and slash with the barbed edges.
Such boots grant the wearer a boost of speed; companions tacitly ignore the little wings on the sides.
What is in the box? No-one knows, but the sounds it produces makes even the bravest flee in mortal terror!
Grim resolve fills the heart of those that hear this clarion.
This wooden and bone chest contains great bounty.
The Shield of the Old Ones grows more powerful under the influence of this glowing plaque.
An ancient vestment enchanted by the eccentric Mage, Folariath.
The most feared of all Elven magical rings is the black iron Ring of Fury, belonging to Khaine, the Bloody-handed God of Murder.
A ring of a wrathful god will make its bearer faster, and more aggressive in his outlook.
The cloak is made from the feathers of the mysterious Coatl, shimmering with a power to ward against dark sorcery.
The bearer of this amethyst amulet knows things no mortal should.
A dark crown, that will ensorcel the heart of those that bear it.
Made from gold of the Blackspine Mountains, the Deathmask depicts Khaine in his aspect of the Deathbringer.
The Emerald Collar is a gold band encrusted with cursed stones.
The size of the artefact known as the Talisman of Saphery belies its power, negating the effects of enchanted weapons against the bearer.
The amulet is a lustrous polished stone with a midnight hue, engraved with a single spiteful rune.
These golden bracers are fabled to have been found on the shores of distant Lustria and are inscribed with unusual glyphs.
To the valiant, this blade lends supernatural speed and vigour; to the craven and corrupt, it brings only swift death.
A dire lance, etched with the fiery blood of Dragons. It is much feared by High Elf Princes from the realm of Caledor.
Trollhide confers some of the more gruesome abilities of its former occupant to the wearer!
This breastplate, inscribed with the Grail Vow, knits otherwise mortal wounds together so its wearer can fight another day.
When woven within a living horse’s mane, hair from Gille’s steed confers strength and resilience into mounts of the same noble bloodline.
Those who don the Armour of Fortune seem to have the favour of Ranald, able to parry the lethal blow with a lucky deflection.
Forged from a rare star metal, it is said that no mortal blade can piece the Armour of Meteoric Iron.
A dingy, battered helmet that looks like any other – but this is the Trickster’s Helm, a powerful artefact that protects the wearer.
An enchanted duo of blades - one long and one short - give the wielder a dazzling array of skilful moves, to parry and deceive an opponent.
The Ogre Blade was used by Chaos Dwarfs to tame the kingdoms amongst the Mountains of Mourn. How it came to the Old World is a mystery.
This blade was stolen from a Tomb Banshee while she sang a haunting nursery tale to a forgotten child. Now the blade sings too, and shrieks when it strikes a foe.
A sword tinged red, for wherever it is swung bloodshed is guaranteed, with multiple foes falling in a single deadly arc.
